column1: # clues.tsv for ft_isalpha -- pedagogic hints only: each line is a QUESTION, never the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><CASE label><TAB>...   (a line fires if ANY of its cases fails)

Which codes does man ascii give the uppercase letters, and which the lowercase ones? And what does p.8 say a classification function returns for a character in its class: any non-zero value, or one value?
Which character sits just before 'A' in man ascii, which just after 'Z', and likewise around 'a' and 'z'? Is one of your bounds off by one?

man ascii lists 128 characters, the last one 0x7f: is a code above it in any class of the "C" locale, the one a program runs in until it calls setlocale()? (man 3 toupper, NOTES, says what that locale knows of umlauts.) Does your class have an upper end, and does your function check it?
Which value does <stdio.h> give EOF, and is that value the code of any character?
Which codes in man ascii are in neither letter range? Does one of them get into your class?
